title: Race Against Time
statementMd:
Have you ever tried to explain to the coordinator, why it is eight hours to the contest and not a single problem has been prepared yet? Misha had. And this time he has a *really* strong excuse: he faced a space-time paradox! Space and time replaced each other.

The entire universe turned into an enormous clock face with three hands — hour, minute, and second. Time froze, and clocks now show the time $*h*$ hours, $*m*$ minutes, $*s*$ seconds.

Last time Misha talked with the coordinator at $*t*_{1}$ o'clock, so now he stands on the number $*t*_{1}$ on the clock face. The contest should be ready by $*t*_{2}$ o'clock. In the terms of paradox it means that Misha has to go to number $*t*_{2}$ somehow. Note that he doesn't have to move forward only: in these circumstances time has no direction.

Clock hands are very long, and Misha cannot get round them. He also cannot step over as it leads to the collapse of space-time. That is, if hour clock points 12 and Misha stands at 11 then he cannot move to 1 along the top arc. He has to follow all the way round the clock center (of course, if there are no other hands on his way).

Given the hands' positions, $*t*_{1}$, and $*t*_{2}$, find if Misha can prepare the contest on time (or should we say *on space*?). That is, find if he can move from $*t*_{1}$ to $*t*_{2}$ by the clock face.

## Input

Five integers $*h*$, $*m*$, $*s*$, $*t*_{1}$, $*t*_{2}$ ($1 ≤ *h* ≤ 12$, $0 ≤ *m*, *s* ≤ 59$, $1 ≤ *t*_{1}, *t*_{2} ≤ 12$, $*t*_{1} ≠ *t*_{2}$).

Misha's position and the target time do not coincide with the position of any hand.

## Output

Print "`YES`" (quotes for clarity), if Misha can prepare the contest on time, and "`NO`" otherwise.

You can print each character either upper- or lowercase ("`YeS`" and "`yes`" are valid when the answer is "`YES`").

## Note

The three examples are shown on the pictures below from left to right. The starting position of Misha is shown with green, the ending position is shown with pink. Note that the positions of the hands on the pictures are not exact, but are close to the exact and the answer is the same.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bce115ce252800c8518f002b1f3de40c04fa0f2d.png)
statementZhMd:
你是否曾试图向协调员解释，为什么距离比赛开始只剩八个小时，却连一道题都还没准备好？Misha 曾经这样做过。而这次，他有一个*非常*充分的理由：他遇到了时空悖论！空间与时间互换了。

整个宇宙变成了一个巨大的钟面，上面有三根指针——时针、分针和秒针。时间凝固了，而时钟现在显示的时间是 $*h*$ 时 $*m*$ 分 $*s*$ 秒。

上一次 Misha 在 $*t*_{1}$ 点与协调员交谈，因此现在他站在钟面上的数字 $*t*_{1}$ 处。比赛应当在 $*t*_{2}$ 点前准备就绪。在悖论的语境下，这意味着 Misha 必须想办法前往数字 $*t*_{2}$ 所在的位置。注意，他不一定只能向前移动：在这种情况下，时间没有方向。

钟的指针非常长，Misha 无法绕过它们。他也不能跨过指针，否则会导致时空坍缩。也就是说，如果时针指向 12，而 Misha 站在 11，那么他不能沿着钟面上方的圆弧移动到 1。他必须绕钟面中心走完整一圈（当然，前提是途中没有其他指针）。

给定指针的位置、$*t*_{1}$ 和 $*t*_{2}$，判断 Misha 能否及时准备好比赛（或者应该说是*及时准备好空间*？）。也就是说，判断他能否沿着钟面从 $*t*_{1}$ 移动到 $*t*_{2}$。

## 输入格式

五个整数 $*h*$、$*m*$、$*s*$、$*t*_{1}$、$*t*_{2}$（$1 ≤ *h* ≤ 12$，$0 ≤ *m*$、$*s* ≤ 59$，$1 ≤ *t*_{1}, *t*_{2} ≤ 12$，$*t*_{1} ≠ *t*_{2}$）。

Misha 的位置和目标时间均不与任何指针的位置重合。

## 输出格式

如果 Misha 能及时准备好比赛，输出 "`YES`"（引号仅为清晰起见），否则输出 "`NO`"。

每个字符的大小写均可任意（当答案为 "`YES`" 时，"`YeS`" 和 "`yes`" 都是合法的）。

## 说明

下面的图片从左到右展示了三个样例。Misha 的起点用绿色表示，终点用粉色表示。注意，图片中指针的位置并不精确，只是接近实际位置，但答案相同。
